text:
The Baesveireach Compact entered the period as a military power defined by its conflict with the Waeslefell Compact. For the first six years, the Compact dominated the field at Thea Seam, winning seven consecutive battles against its rival while launching raids that carried off plunder. This era of external aggression ended in year 10 with a peace treaty that left both sides exhausted. The internal stability of the Compact was equally fragile; succession followed the rule of the strongest, a mechanism that produced immediate violence. When Sildbeld Bouthwoun died in year 13, Kramboul Dend took the seat by setting aside the named heir Fur Roundpoull, who was cast out. The Compact’s standing deteriorated rapidly, leading to the loss of Thea Seam in year 16 and a devastating plague in Baesveireach that killed 530 people and displaced 407 others.

The latter half of the period was marked by the collapse of the Compact’s territorial integrity and the violent turnover of its leadership. After a brief recovery, the Waeslefell Compact declared war in year 26, reversing the earlier balance of power. The Baesveireach Compact lost three battles, including the loss of its capital, Baesveireach, in year 29. Leadership changed hands twice through assassination: Bage Busba was killed by Steapall Faedild in year 28, and Steapall Faedild was killed by Ground Raeskur in year 29. Steapall Faedild briefly held the seat after setting aside the named heir Drourn Nethi, but the power was effectively destroyed. The period ended in year 30 with a peace treaty that acknowledged the collapse of the Baesveireach Compact.

Over the twenty-seven years, the Compact held the seat for four people, each ruling for an average of 6.2 years. It fought ten battles against the Waeslefell Compact, winning seven and losing three. It launched five raids, two of which carried off plunder and three of which were beaten off. It suffered one raid, which also resulted in plunder for the attacker. The internal cost of its rule included two murders committed by its own people and two castings out of losing claimants. Two exiles returned to service, and three people were courted away from its ruler. The Compact lost two places, Thea Seam and Baesveireach, to the Waeslefell Compact. The period concluded with the power finished, its leadership extinguished and its territory seized.

The Skomere Charter began its final years as a fragment of a larger whole, having been carved from the Waeslefell Compact in year 47. Touthseand Gourses, who had carried off two places to establish the new power, held the seat as the period opened. The entity’s existence was defined by this recent separation and the precariousness of its hold on the territory it had seized.

The stability of the Charter was undermined by the return of exiles in its later years. In year 50, Nounmam Mith returned from exile and took service with the Skomere Charter. This was followed in year 51 by the return of Meirnhaes Kould, who also took service with the power. These arrivals marked the end of the period, with the Charter still holding the seat but now integrated with figures who had previously been cast out.

Free Kremoor spent its twenty-four years from 28 to 51 as a fragile entity, born from the Deafil League and sustained by the return of exiles who repeatedly challenged its leadership. Feinnind Keitrith held the seat from the start in 28, ruling for 16 years before his rule ended when he was cast out in 44. His tenure was marked by internal violence and the defection of key figures to the Waeslefell Compact. Nounmam Mith succeeded him in 44, holding the seat for five years until he too was cast out in 49. Til Saeld took the seat in 49 and remained in power when the period ended. The power never expanded its territory, sending five raids that were all beaten off, while losing two of its own rulers to attempted murder.

Feinnind Keitrith’s long rule began with the return of exiles Staellou Keillthae, Touthseand Gourses, Vamkei Dridrill, Ground Raeskur, and Sealdvern Geitoun, who all took service with Free Kremoor. Despite this influx, internal strife erupted early. In 35, Staellou Keillthae challenged Feinnind Keitrith openly for the seat, lost, and was killed by Feinnind Keitrith at Kremoor. This violence did not stabilize the regime. In 37, Ground Raeskur abandoned Free Kremoor for the Waeslefell Compact, prompting a failed raid on Waeslefell. Later, Sealdvern Geitoun attempted to murder Feinnind Keitrith in 39 and was cast out, only to be declared an outlaw in 40 after a conspiracy was uncovered. Feinnind Keitrith himself attempted to murder Greandsam Kreir in 44, leading to his own casting out.

Nounmam Mith took the seat by election in 44, bringing Nounmam Mith’s own exile into the fold. His rule was short and ended in similar fashion. In 49, he attempted to murder Woum Teldlei, failed, and was cast out. Til Saeld, raised from Kremoor with no remaining claimant, took the seat in 49. The power’s external posture remained consistently defensive; it sent raids against Thea Seam, Fa Cut, Waeslefell, and Skomere, all of which were beaten off. No raids got through, and no plunder was carried off. The period ended with Til Saeld still holding the seat, having inherited a power that had lost two rulers to internal violence and seen seven exiles return, yet failing to secure its borders or its internal loyalty.

The period from 33 to 51 saw Greater Baesveireach shift from a state of territorial expansion to one of internal consolidation and external vulnerability. At the start, Rearn Thill held the seat and expanded the power’s reach by taking two places from the Waeslefell Compact in 33. The power’s standing was defined by its inability to project force outward, as all four raids it sent out between 38 and 43 were beaten off. Simultaneously, it suffered two raids from the Waeslefell Compact in 41 and 42, which carried off plunder and killed people. The period ended with Feinnind Keitrith still holding the seat, having seized power through violence after Rearn Thill’s death.

Rearn Thill’s rule was marked by defensive failures and the loss of territory. After swearing an alliance with Free Kremoor in 35, Greater Baesveireach attempted to raid Thea Seam in 38 and Fa Cut in 39, both of which were beaten off. In 42, a raid on Waeslefell was also beaten off, while the Waeslefell Compact raided Weisfaewick, killing 49 people. The power’s internal stability fractured in 48 when Feinnind Keitrith, who had returned from exile in 45, had Rearn Thill murdered at Baesveireach. Feinnind Keitrith took the seat by right of birth, ending Rearn Thill’s rule.

Feinnind Keitrith’s tenure was characterized by purges and the return of exiles. He had Sealdvern Geitoun murdered at Waeslefell in 47 and Woum Teldlei murdered at Waeslefell in 49. Despite the internal violence, the power saw three exiles return to take service: Feinnind Keitrith in 45, Noulldou Beivourn in 49, and Full Sanweil in 51. The seat passed from Rearn Thill to Feinnind Keitrith one time. Rearn Thill was killed, and Feinnind Keitrith was still holding the seat at the end of the period.

The Waeslefell Compact’s decade was defined by violent succession and rapid disintegration. It began with Nounmam Mith holding the seat, a position he lost in 42 when Greandsam Kreir challenged him openly and took power. The period saw six different rulers, each holding the seat for an average of 1.5 years, with the seat passing five times. The Compact’s authority eroded from internal murder and contested claims to external rebellion, ending with Haeth Tha taking the seat in 51 while the power itself remained intact but diminished.

Greandsam Kreir ruled from 42 until his murder in 47 by Thraebaern Ramdem at Skomere. During his rule, the Compact sent one raid on Weisfaewick, carrying off 41 grain and killing 49, while beating off raids from Greater Baesveireach on Waeslefell and Skomere. After Kreir’s death, Noulldou Beivourn took the seat by setting aside the claim of the named heir Touthseand Gourses. This contest split the Compact: Touthseand Gourses carried off two places, Skomere and Thea Seam, to form the Skomere Charter. Noulldou Beivourn was cast out in 48 by Woum Teldlei, who had challenged him openly.

Woum Teldlei’s rule ended when he was killed by Feinnind Keitrith in 49. Ronith Wasnur then took the seat, setting aside the claim of the named heir Meirnhaes Kould, who was cast out. Ronith’s tenure was marked by instability; he faced an attempted murder by Gandkim Kiveald and a conspiracy by Full Sanweil, both of whom were cast out. In 50, Seithfum Mim married Til Saeld, binding the Compact to Free Kremoor. Ronith died in 51 at age 18. Haeth Tha took the seat that year, setting aside the claim of the named heir Thraebaern Ramdem, who was cast out.

The Compact suffered significant losses beyond leadership changes. A plague at Skomere in 46 and 47 killed 176 people and caused 176 others to flee. Fa Cut rose against the Compact in 48 after its standing had fallen to nothing, though Free Kremoor’s raid on Fa Cut in 51 was beaten off. The Compact’s own people murdered from within totaled one, and six people were cast out for various reasons. Two marriages tied the Compact to Free Kremoor. The period ended with Haeth Tha holding the seat, having survived the turbulent succession of the previous decade.

The Deafil League’s thirty-four years were defined by a cycle of binding alliances and violent isolation. It began in year 2 bound to the Baesveireach Compact through the marriages of Featrein Roumi, Hou Lae, Bage Busba, Kramboul Dend, Kae Voth, and Drourn Nethi. These ties held until year 27, when Sealdvern Geitoun married Sundsea Pim, shifting the League’s allegiance to the Waeslefell Compact. The period ended with the League finished, its land lost and its followers scattered, after a war with the Waeslefell Compact that lasted one year.

The League’s internal stability was fragile, marked by five rulers who held the seat for an average of 6.4 years each. Feasleith Husbill died in year 11, leading to an election where Steapall Faedild took the seat, casting out the named heir Bage Busba. Steapall Faedild ruled until year 23, when Fur Roundpoull challenged him openly and won the seat. Fur Roundpoull’s rule ended in year 28 when Sealdvern Geitoun challenged him and took the seat by coup. Sealdvern Geitoun was cast out in year 29 for an attempted murder on Ground Raeskur. Deththou Keis then took the seat in year 29 by election, setting aside the named heir Touthseand Gourses. His house ended when the League was finished. Five people were cast out during this time: Bage Busba, Steapall Faedild, Fur Roundpoull, Sealdvern Geitoun, and Touthseand Gourses.

External conflicts escalated from raiding to total destruction. The Waeslefell Compact raided Kremoor in year 8 and Skomere in year 9, prompting retaliatory raids by the Deafil League on Waeslefell and Weisfaewick. The League sent eight raids in total; two carried off plunder, one got through but took nothing, and five were beaten off. The League suffered four raids from the Waeslefell Compact, all carrying off plunder. In year 24, Kremoor rose against the League as its standing had fallen very low. In year 28, Kremoor broke from the League as Free Kremoor. The League fought one battle, lost to the Waeslefell Compact at Skomere in year 34, losing 179 men and the place itself. The League was finished in year 34, and peace was made in year 35.

The Waeslefell Compact’s twenty-year span from 22 to 41 was defined by a violent succession, a protracted war with the Baesveireach Compact, and a final collapse of authority that left its ruler dead and its standing ruined. The period began with Vaell Foull holding the seat, a position he lost when Ground Raeskur had him murdered at Skomere in 24. Ground Raeskur took the seat by right of birth, but his rule was immediately challenged by internal conspiracies and external warfare. He survived an attempt on his life by Staellou Keillthae in 28, who was cast out and later declared an outlaw. Ground Raeskur himself was cast out in 32 after losing an open challenge to Fur Roundpoull.

Fur Roundpoull ruled for one year before dying in Waeslefell in 33. His death triggered a contest between Rontaen Sin and the named heir Rearn Thill. Rontaen Sin took the seat, setting aside Rearn Thill’s claim, and the Compact was divided, with Rearn Thill carrying off two places as Greater Baesveireach. Rontaen Sin’s rule ended in 36 when Nounmam Mith had him murdered at Waeslefell. Deththou Keis took the seat by right of birth, but Nounmam Mith challenged him in 37, won, and took the seat by coup, casting Deththou Keis out. Nounmam Mith held the seat until the end of the period.

The Compact’s military history was dominated by its war with the Baesveireach Compact, which lasted four years. The Compact lost one battle at Thea Seam in 26, with 36 dead, but won three others: at Thea Seam in 27 with 30 dead, and at Baesveireach in 28 and 29 with 82 and 66 dead respectively. It took Thea Seam and Baesveireach from the Baesveireach Compact. The Compact also fought the Deafil League, defeating it at Skomere in 34 with 179 dead and taking the settlement, which led to the Deafil League’s destruction. The Compact sent two raids, both carrying off plunder, and suffered nine raids, all of which were beaten off.

Internal stability eroded throughout the period. Six years of hunger at Thea Seam killed 23 people and caused 60 to flee. The Compact’s standing fell to nothing, leading Thea Seam to rise against it in 35. Nine people were courted away from its ruler. The Compact’s rule ended with Nounmam Mith still holding the seat, but the power had lost two places to Greater Baesveireach and its authority was broken.

The Waeslefell Compact’s twenty-year span from 2 to 21 was defined by a war it lost and a seat it could not hold. It began by occupying Fa Cut in 2, but its standing collapsed after a marriage to the Baesveireach Compact in 3 turned into a declaration of war for Thea Seam in 4. The Compact fought six battles against the Baesveireach Compact, all lost at Thea Seam, with casualties ranging from 26 dead in 4 to 8 dead in 9. The conflict ended in 10 with both sides exhausted.

Internal decay followed the war. Famine struck Fa Cut repeatedly, killing 302 people and driving 147 from their homes. Keirn Heapound died in 10, and Vaell Foull took the seat by right of birth. His rule was unstable; Grefraem Meheath attempted to murder him in 11 and was cast out, then declared an outlaw. In 13, Vor Saern challenged Vaell Foull openly, won, and took the seat. Vaell Foull was cast out, and Fa Cut rose against the Compact, whose standing had fallen to nothing.

Vor Saern ruled until his death in 17. Vaell Foull took the seat again by right of birth. The Compact raided Kremoor in 8, 18, and Skomere in 9, 19, carrying off plunder each time. It suffered ten raids, four of which were beaten off. The period ended with Vaell Foull still holding the seat, having survived the loss of six battles, the death of two rulers, and the exile of one challenger.

Til Saeld assumed the seat of Free Kremoor in 49, following the exile of Nounmam Mith. Mith had been cast out after an attempt on the life of Woum Teldlei failed and was traced to him. With no claimant remaining, Saeld was raised from Kremoor to hold the power.

The period concluded with a military failure. In 51, Free Kremoor launched a raid on Fa Cut, which was beaten off.

In year 51, Ronith Wasnur, the ruler of the Waeslefell Compact, died in Waeslefell. Haeth Tha contested the claim of Thraebaern Ramdem, the named heir, to the seat of the Waeslefell Compact. Haeth Tha took the seat, setting aside the claim of Thraebaern Ramdem.

Thraebaern Ramdem was cast out of the Waeslefell Compact. During this same year, a raid by Free Kremoor on Fa Cut was beaten off.

The Waeslefell Compact declared war on the Baesveireach Compact in 26 over a long-standing grievance. The Baesveireach Compact and its allies defeated the Waeslefell Compact at Thea Seam in 26, killing 36. The Waeslefell Compact reversed this outcome at Thea Seam in 27, killing 30, and took the site from the Baesveireach Compact.

In 28, the Waeslefell Compact defeated the Baesveireach Compact at Baesveireach, killing 82. In 29, Ground Raeskur had Steapall Faedild murdered at Baesveireach. The Waeslefell Compact defeated the Baesveireach Compact at Baesveireach later that year, killing 66, and took the settlement from the Baesveireach Compact.

The war ended in 30 when the two powers made peace after 4 years. The peace followed the collapse of the Baesveireach Compact.

The war began in year 4 when the Waeslefell Compact declared war on the Baesveireach Compact for control of Thea Seam. The Baesveireach Compact and its allies defeated the Waeslefell Compact at Thea Seam in year 4, with 26 dead. The Baesveireach Compact and its allies defeated the Waeslefell Compact at Thea Seam in year 5, with 20 dead. The Baesveireach Compact and its allies defeated the Waeslefell Compact at Thea Seam in year 6, with 13 dead. The Baesveireach Compact and its allies defeated the Waeslefell Compact at Thea Seam in year 7, with 11 dead. The Baesveireach Compact and its allies defeated the Waeslefell Compact at Thea Seam in year 8, with 9 dead. The Baesveireach Compact and its allies defeated the Waeslefell Compact at Thea Seam in year 9, with 8 dead.

The conflict ended in year 10 when the Waeslefell Compact and the Baesveireach Compact made peace after 6 years, both sides exhausted.
